title: A finitely generated ideal contained in the radical of I has a power contained in I
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian ring R and ideals I, J with J contained in the radical of I, the lemma asserts the existence of an exponent n with J^n contained in I, and consequently that locally nilpotent ideals are nilpotent in the Noetherian case (statement lines 6516-6527). The proof does not iterate powers of J or invoke primary decomposition: it unwinds the radical membership on the finitely many generators of J to get exponents d_i, and then takes n = d_1 + ... + d_s + 1, the length at which every monomial in the generators is forced to contain one f_i to the power d_i (proof lines 6529-6533). The finite generation of J is what makes this possible, and that is exactly where the Noetherian hypothesis enters; the author writes the whole argument out in three sentences. H2.
